brief: A Bloomberg gauge of global sovereign bond yields rose to 3.72%, the highest since mid-2008, with Japan, UK, Australia and US 10-year yields also hitting multi-decade or multi-year highs. First Eagle's Appio says markets are pricing a higher path for short rates as investors reassess the neutral rate upward. JPMorgan's Hanelin ties the move to three drivers: Middle East conflict pushing oil higher (clients selling curve butterflies); Warsh's savings-to-investment framing implying r-star is higher than priced, leaving valuations rich; and a market view that treats military action as bond-market intervention, so the conflict and energy prices drive long-end volatility. Goldman's Privorotsky frames the AI investment boom as bullish equities but bearish duration, since AI capex and hyperscaler issuance crowd out Treasury supply for savings; Treasury buybacks helped temporarily but did not reverse the trend. Goldman also ties diesel to over 40% of a $40/bbl rise in refined product prices since February, linked to a 25% YoY export decline. TD Securities and Nuveen expect the selloff to continue on fiscal deterioration and higher term premium; Nomura calls gold the release valve.
